items.title: 11.3 Reaction mechanism and modes of bond breaking

source_refs.note: Topic 11.3 with Figures 11.5 and 11.6, printed pages 251-252.

blocks.text: Reaction mechanism is the series of steps that take place in the course of the overall reaction. Like all chemical reactions, organic reactions involve the breaking of chemical bonds. There are two ways in which covalent bonds can break.
Homolytic fission occurs when the covalent bond breaks evenly to produce free radicals.

blocks.title: Free Radical
blocks.text: Free Radical is a species that contains an unpaired electron and is very reactive.
Free radicals are extremely reactive because of the tendency of unpaired electrons to become paired.

blocks.alt: Boxed heading Homolytic Cleavage. A-B with two half-headed (fish-hook) arrows from the bond, one to each atom, then an arrow marked Homolysis to A. + B., labelled Free radicals. Below: Cl-Cl with two fish-hook arrows, an arrow marked hv, giving Cl. + Cl., labelled Free radicals.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.5: Homolytic fission and free radical formation (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.5).

blocks.text: Heterolytic fission occurs when the covalent bond breaks in such a way that the originally shared pair of electrons is gained by one atom only and oppositely child ions are produced. This bond fission is shown by full curly arrows in mechanisms.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: ‘Oppositely child ions’ is a misprint for oppositely charged ions: one atom keeps both electrons and becomes negative, the other becomes positive.

blocks.alt: Boxed heading Heterolytic cleavage. A-B with the bonding pair of electrons circled and a full curly arrow from it to B, giving A+ and :B-. Below: H3C-Cl with three lone pairs on Cl and a curly arrow from the C-Cl bond to Cl, giving the H3C+ ion and the chloride ion :Cl:- with four lone pairs.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.6: Heterolytic fission and formation of ions (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.6).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed caption reads 'formation of radical ions'. Heterolytic fission gives ions (a carbocation and a chloride ion), not radicals, so the caption above reads 'formation of ions'.
